title: Liu Bei Entrusts His Son at Baidi; Five Armies Are Turned Back
summary: Dying at Baidi, Liu Bei says the thing that has been argued about ever since: if his son is worth supporting, support him — and if he is not, take the throne yourself. Zhuge Liang puts his head on the floor and weeps until it bleeds.

Cao Pi sends five armies at once against a leaderless Shu. Zhuge Liang, who has not left his residence in days and is found feeding fish in his garden, has already turned four of them back without a battle.
history: The deathbed offer is in the histories, word for word. Whether it was sincere or the most elegant loyalty test ever devised is the oldest argument in the field.

pins.note: 'If he is not worth it, take the throne yourself.'
Sends five armies, and gets none of them home.
Holds the western road by existing.
